FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; no experiment has been executed and none is claimed)

Title: Extracting and Analyzing Basic Molecular Properties from a Chemical Dataset

═══════════════════════════════════════════
1. OBJECTIVE
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Design a reproducible pipeline that (a) ingests a chemical dataset of molecular structures, (b) computes a panel of basic physicochemical properties per molecule, (c) validates the computed values against known references, and (d) produces a quantitative descriptive analysis of the property distributions. The deliverable is the design itself; execution is out of scope for this task.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
2. DATA SOURCES — TWO EXPLICIT BRANCHES
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Because the /workspace repository contains no chemical data, the design defines two first-class, mutually exclusive branches selected at pipeline start:

BRANCH A — Supplied dataset (preferred, conditional on availability).
- Input: a structure table (CSV/TSV/SDF) with one structure identifier column (SMILES or InChI) plus optional metadata columns (e.g., name, class, source, measured logP).
- Pre-ingest profiling: record file size, row count, column names/types, fraction of rows with parseable structures, and provenance metadata (source, version, citation) if supplied. Provenance is recorded verbatim in the validation report; if absent, it is logged as "unknown" (see Uncertainties).
- Salt/mixture policy (declared up front): for multi-component records (salts, solvates), retain the largest organic fragment (RDKit `rdMolDescriptors.CalcMolFormula` on `Chem.GetMolFrags(..., asMols=True, sanitizeFrags=True)` largest by heavy-atom count) and log discarded fragments.

BRANCH B — Embedded reference set (fallback; exercised when no dataset is available).
- A curated in-code table of ~20 well-characterized molecules with published property values, e.g.: ethanol (MW 46.069, logP −0.31), benzene (78.114, logP 1.68), aspirin (180.158, logP 1.19, TPSA 63.6 Å² — see control thresholds), caffeine (194.19, logP −0.07, TPSA 58.44 Å²), ibuprofen (206.28, logP 3.97), paracetamol (151.16, logP 0.46, TPSA 49.3 Å²), glucose, benzoic acid, glycine, cholesterol, DDT, penicillin G, etc. Each entry carries: canonical SMILES, expected MW (4 dp), expected formula, expected TPSA (1 dp), expected cLogP (2 dp), expected HBD/HBA.
- Rationale: guarantees the pipeline is fully demonstrable and its controls verifiable even with no external data; every Branch-B run doubles as a validation run because expected values are known. Branch B does not support population-level distributional claims — outputs are labeled "pipeline validation output" rather than "dataset analysis."
- Both branches share the identical compute/validate/analyze code path; only the ingestion module differs. The run manifest records which branch was taken and why.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
3. PROPERTY PANEL (per molecule)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
Computed via RDKit (tools/methods rationale: RDKit is the de-facto open-source standard, deterministic, and implements the named algorithms):
1. Exact MW (CalcExactMolWt) and average MW (Descripts.MolWt)
2. Molecular formula (CalcMolFormula)
3. Heavy-atom count
4. cLogP — Wildman–Crippen method (Crippen.MolLogP)
5. TPSA — Ertl method (rdMolDescriptors.CalcTPSA)
6. H-bond donors / acceptors — Lipinski definitions (Lipinski.NumHDonors / NumHAcceptors)
7. Rotatable bonds (Lipinski.NumRotatableBonds)
8. Formal charge (Chem.GetFormalCharge)
9. Ring count and aromatic-ring count (Lipinski.RingCount / rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumAromaticRings)
10. Fraction sp³ (rdMolDescriptors.CalcFractionCsp3)
11. Lipinski RO5 flags (MW>500, logP>5, HBD>5, HBA>10) and Veber flags (rotatable bonds>10, TPSA>140)
12. Structural identity: canonical SMILES and InChI (for deduplication and round-trip checks)

Fallback tooling (only if RDKit is unavailable at execution time — see Uncertainties): a pure-Python path computing element-count MW and formula exactly (from a parsed molecular formula or minimal SMILES atom parser), HBD/HBA by simple donor/acceptor atom patterns, and flagging cLogP/TPSA as "not computable (tooling unavailable)" rather than approximating them. This reduced-fidelity path must be explicitly labeled in outputs.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
4. CONTROLS & SANITY CHECKS (with acceptance thresholds)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
All checks are executed on every run and compiled into a machine-readable validation report (JSON) with pass/fail per check.

C1. Reference-value check (Branch B always; Branch A: also run the embedded reference set as a self-test before processing the supplied data).
  - Tolerances: |ΔMW| ≤ 0.05 Da (average MW) and ≤ 0.001 Da (exact MW); formula exact string match; |ΔTPSA| ≤ 0.5 Å²; |ΔcLogP| ≤ 0.10; HBD/HBA exact integer match. Acceptance: ≥ 95% of reference molecules pass ALL fields; any MW mismatch is an automatic hard fail (MW is deterministic given a correct structure).
C2. SMILES round-trip: canonical SMILES re-parsed and re-canonicalized must be identical. Acceptance: 100% of valid molecules; any failure invalidates that record.
C3. Formula–MW consistency: average MW recomputed from the parsed formula's element counts × standard atomic weights must match descriptor output. Acceptance: |Δ| ≤ 0.02 Da for 100% of molecules.
C4. Salt/fragment accounting: for every multi-fragment record, log the number of discarded fragments and their heavy-atom counts; acceptance: no silent discards (every discard appears in the report).
C5. Deduplication: duplicate detection via canonical SMILES; report exact duplicate count and conflict rate (duplicates with differing metadata).
C6. Plausible-range screen (flags, not failures): MW outside [10, 1000] Da, cLogP outside [−5, 10], TPSA outside [0, 400] Å², formal charge outside [−4, +4] → flagged as outliers with values reported; acceptance is transparency, not exclusion (a flag rate > 10% triggers a data-quality warning in the report).
C7. Parse accounting: invalid/empty structure records counted; acceptance: parse-failure rate reported; if > 5%, dataset quality is flagged.
C8. Determinism check: pipeline re-run on a 100-molecule random subset must reproduce identical values bit-for-bit.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
5. ANALYSIS PLAN (quantified)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
- Descriptive statistics per property: n, mean, median, SD, IQR, min, max, and count of missing values. Reported to 2–3 significant figures appropriate to each property's precision.
- Distributions: histogram and box plot for MW, cLogP, TPSA, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds; bin edges specified (MW: 25 Da bins; cLogP: 0.5-unit bins; TPSA: 10 Å² bins).
- Correlations: Spearman (primary, robust to skew) and Pearson (secondary) among {MW, cLogP, TPSA, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, fraction sp³}; report r with 95% CI (bootstrap, 1,000 resamples, fixed seed 42) and Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment across the pairwise matrix. Expected qualitative directions to check as internal sanity (e.g., MW vs. TPSA positively correlated; HBD vs. cLogP weakly negative) — deviations are noted, not treated as failures.
- Drug-likeness summary: % of molecules passing all four Lipinski criteria, % passing Veber, and a crosstab of individual violations.
- Stratified analysis (Branch A only, if a class/source metadata column exists): per-group medians with Kruskal–Wallis test across ≥3 groups (α = 0.05) and effect size (epsilon-squared); no group comparison is performed if no metadata column exists.
- Outlier narrative: top/bottom 5 molecules by MW, cLogP, and TPSA listed with structures.
- Deliverables: (i) per-molecule property CSV (one row per unique molecule); (ii) summary statistics table; (iii) correlation matrix with CIs; (iv) figure set (PNG/SVG); (v) validation report JSON from §4; (vi) run manifest (branch taken, tool versions, RDKit release, timestamp, random seed).

═══════════════════════════════════════════
6. FEASIBILITY
═══════════════════════════════════════════
- Compute: property computation is O(molecules × descriptors); ~10^4 molecules complete in seconds, 10^6 in minutes single-core; well within available resources (224 CPU cores reported).
- Tooling risk: the current sandbox has Python 3.14.4 with no RDKit/pandas/numpy/scipy, an empty pip cache, and disabled networking — dependencies cannot be installed here. The design therefore requires either (i) an execution environment with RDKit available, or (ii) use of the explicitly defined pure-Python fallback path (§3), which yields a reduced property panel (MW, formula, HBD/HBA, counts; no cLogP/TPSA).
- Data risk: no dataset exists in the repository; Branch B guarantees the pipeline is always executable, but any population-level conclusions require Branch A.
- All analyses use standard statistics (SciPy/pandas or hand-rolled equivalents in the fallback); no GPU needed.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
7. ASSUMPTIONS (held as assumptions, not asserted facts)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
A1. A molecular dataset with structure identifiers (SMILES/InChI) will be available at execution time (Branch A), or the embedded reference set (Branch B) is an acceptable demonstration vehicle.
A2. RDKit, or an equivalent cheminformatics toolkit, can be made available in the execution environment.
A3. "Basic molecular properties" refers to the physicochemical descriptor panel in §3 rather than quantum-chemical properties (HOMO/LUMO, etc.).
A4. Computed values such as cLogP and TPSA are model-based predictions, not measurements; any comparison against "measured" logP metadata would treat computed values as estimates with expected deviation.
A5. Reference values in Branch B are correct as tabulated from standard published sources (CRC/DrugBank-style values); if a discrepancy arises, the control failure is investigated rather than the tolerance widened silently.

═══════════════════════════════════════════
8. UNCERTAINTIES (unresolvable from the repository)
═══════════════════════════════════════════
U1. Dataset provenance and population: no data exists locally — source, license, size, and column schema are unknown; whether property columns already exist (vs. must be computed from structures) is unknown.
U2. Intended comparison: whether the analysis targets a single population or a comparison between defined groups is unspecified; the stratified analysis is conditional.
U3. Tooling: RDKit installability in the execution environment cannot be verified from this sandbox; the fallback path has reduced fidelity.
U4. Salt/mixture handling policy and whether predicted vs. experimental values are expected may need researcher confirmation before execution.
U5. Exact molecule list and reference values for the Branch-B embedded set would be finalized at implementation time against a citable source.

No experiment has been run; all numbers above are design specifications (reference constants and thresholds), not results.
